saved_context.user_goal: Implement an in-repo CUDA kernel that is functionally aligned with flashinfer.trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe and faster than that FlashInfer baseline on the real TP=1 G11 workload.
saved_context.baseline: Real flashinfer.trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe, not the PyTorch reference.
saved_context.candidate_rule: The candidate must not call flashinfer.trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe as its implementation.

routing_decomposition.conclusion: Routing pack is not the main remaining gap; the candidate needs tensor-core grouped GEMM and finalize/scatter alignment.

negative_probe_evidence.generic_cutlass_mm_fp4: Works for ordinary dense NVFP4 GEMM on SM103, but directly feeding real G11 prepared gemm1 tensors produced non-finite output.
negative_probe_evidence.standalone_trtllm_mm_fp4: Callable after a local FlashInfer JIT include workaround, but returned non-finite output on real G11 prepared stage1 tensors.
negative_probe_evidence.conclusion: Generic dense mm_fp4 APIs are not drop-in replacements for the fused MoE prepared layout path.

flashinfer_source_map.key_contract: Build expanded_idx_to_permuted_idx, permuted_idx_to_token_idx, cta_idx_xy_to_batch_idx, cta_idx_xy_to_mn_limit, num_non_exiting_ctas, and total_num_padded_tokens for TensorRT-LLM MoE grouped GEMMs.

next_step.description: Add a CUDA extension entry point that converts topk_packed int32 [T, top_k] into the TensorRT-LLM fused MoE routing metadata, validate it against a Python reproduction of FlashInfer routing rules, then use that metadata to pursue a tensor-core grouped GEMM implementation instead of the current scalar/software FP4 FMA path.
